title: Encrypted SQLite snapshot store with transactional mutation
description: Spec §6.1-6.3. One encrypted logical snapshot per vault in ward.db (0600) under ~/.ward (0700); immediate transactions, revision increment, rollback on failure, bounded busy timeout, no plaintext index, SQL tracing off.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T05 (store slice): synthetic plaintext is absent from database, journals and sidecars after create/update/delete and forced failures
T06: concurrent writes preserve both updates or report conflict; an interrupted write leaves the last committed snapshot valid
T07: directory/file modes and ownership enforced; symlink and path-traversal inputs rejected

finalSummary: WCLI-6: the encrypted SQLite snapshot store. What changed: a VaultStore port (src/application/vault-store.ts) and a bun:sqlite adapter (src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts) holding one sealed row per vault in ward.db under ~/.ward; exact-schema recognition with application_id/user_version; immediate-transaction mutations with a synchronous change so no network request can run inside a write transaction; a bounded 5 s busy timeout; 0700/0600 mode, uid and link enforcement with inherited-ACL stripping on creation; refusal of WAL-class headers before any SQLite open; six vault_* catalogue codes that never carry paths or SQL text; an ADR 0001 store-layout consequence. Why: spec §6.1-6.3, gates T05-T07 for the store slice. Verified: 39 store tests in a 217-test suite, green locally (bun 1.3.14, SQLite 3.54.0) and on CI run 36472616615 at head ad7b96b. Controls: removing the mutate transaction fails the concurrency test; an always-conflicting store fails the ok>0 floor; a deferred transaction fails the change-never-ran pin; disabling the header check fails exactly the two WAL-refusal tests; the T05 scan has a planted-sentinel positive control. Independent review (spec §15): four rounds; the reviewer verified every fix empirically and reported no remaining findings. Stated limits: rollback is not detected; SQLite's mandatory hot-journal recovery may modify a file left mid-transaction; pre-existing ACLs are not detected; several connection settings are reviewed defense-in-depth rather than individually pinned; the concurrent-create test pins the outcome pair, not lock timing. Not done here: wiring into commands (WCLI-20) and packaged-binary qualification (WCLI-15).
